title: A merge node joins several lines into one arrow
body:
Today each connector has one `from` and one `to`. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` shows the four threads' results joining into one table. It draws four `sweep` nodes with no head that meet at one point, then a fifth arrow from that point into the table. The meeting point is worked out by hand.

## Proposal

A node `merge` takes several `from` ends and one `to`. Each `from` draws a line, in its own stroke if one is given, into a junction. The junction sits at `at`, or a fixed distance above `to` by default. One arrow runs from the junction to `to`, with the head and label properties of an `arrow`.

```text
merge { from strip1 bottom k1; from strip2 bottom k2; from strip3 bottom k3;
    from strip4 bottom k4; to ranks top; label "merge occupancy"; }
```

## Open

- Whether a property may repeat, as `from` does here, or the ends go in one property.
- How each branch gets its own colour.
- Whether `split`, one end fanning out to several, is the same node reversed.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Jack accepted on 2026-11-23, provisionally: `merge` takes a repeated `from`, as an exception for this node only. `split` comes later as its own node.
